title: Experiencing the Unconditional Love of God | Sri Daya Mata

# Experiencing the Unconditional Love of God

### By Sri Daya Mata
#### Beloved Third President of Self-Realization Fellowship / Yogoda Satsanga Society of India

My dear ones, from the very beginning of creation, the one underlying motivation behind every human activity, every search, and every desire is the soul's deep, eternal hunger for love. We seek it in friendship, we seek it in family, we seek it in our ambitions and creative endeavors. Yet, so often we find ourselves disappointed, because human love, by its very nature, is limited and subject to change. It is only when we begin to realize that the ultimate object of our search is the Infinite, that we find the key to true fulfillment. The supreme Truth of existence is that you are eternally loved by your Creator, and that His love is completely, absolutely unconditional.

Our beloved Guru, Paramahansa Yogananda, often reminded us that God is not a harsh judge sitting in the heavens, waiting to punish us for our mistakes. Rather, the Divine is the most tender, compassionate Father, Mother, Friend, and Beloved. When we look at God through the eyes of devotion, we see that Her love—the love of the Divine Mother—is a boundless ocean that no human error can ever diminish.

> "The love of God, the love of the Divine Mother, is unconditional. It does not depend upon your worthiness; it depends only upon your willingness to open your heart to receive it. She does not look upon your mistakes; She looks only at your desire to return to Her."

---

### The Silent Cry of the Soul

Every soul is seeking a love that never fades, a love that understands our deepest weaknesses and yet loves us unconditionally. In the quiet moments of your life, when the noise of the world fades away, there is a silent cry within you. It is the cry of the child calling out for its mother. This is the natural relationship we share with the Divine. 

We often make the mistake of thinking we must become perfect before we can approach God. But our Guru, Paramahansa Yogananda, taught us that this is not true. If a child falls in the mud, does the mother abandon him? No, she runs to pick him up, washes his soiled clothes, and holds him close to her heart. In the same way, the Divine Mother is ever-ready to lift us up from the mire of worldly delusion. All She asks is that we turn our gaze back to Her, with child-like trust and simplicity.

### Finding the Divine Mother Within

To experience this unconditional love, we must cultivate the habit of going within. Meditation is the science of attuning the soul to the Infinite. When we sit in the silence of deep meditation, withdrawing our senses from the external world, we begin to feel a great peace. That peace is the first whisper of the Divine Presence. 

Sri Daya Mata often recalled how her Gurudeva taught her to pray. He would say, "Do not pray with dry, intellectual words. Speak to God in the language of your own heart. Talk to Her as you would to your own mother, with absolute sincerity. Tell Her: 'Mother, naughty or good, I am Thy child. Thou must come to me. Thou must reveal Thyself to me.'"

When we pray in this way, with dynamic will and intense yearning, we tear away the veil of cosmic delusion. The Divine Mother cannot resist the sincere, loving demand of Her child. Her love flows into our consciousness, filling us with a joy so profound that no earthly experience can compare.

### Transforming Daily Life Into a Sanctuary

To keep this divine connection alive, we must learn to bring the peace of our meditation into our daily activities. It is not enough to feel close to God only when we are sitting on our meditation cushions. We must practice His presence throughout the day. 

Whether you are working in an office, caring for your family, or performing chores, keep a corner of your mind always anchored in the Divine. This is the practice of Japa—the silent, continuous repetition of God's name or a sacred affirmation. By maintaining this inner dialogue with the Lord, you build a fortress of peace around your soul that nothing in this world can disturb.

### Practical Habits for Attuning to Divine Love

To deepen your experience of God's unconditional love, incorporate these simple, practical spiritual habits into your daily life:

* **Begin and End the Day with God:** Dedicate the first moments of your morning and the last moments of your evening to silent prayer and communion. Let your last thought before sleep be: *"I love Thee, Lord; Thou art with me."*
* **Practice Child-like Surrender:** Whenever you make a mistake or feel overwhelmed, do not indulge in self-condemnation. Instead, immediately hand your worries over to the Divine Mother. Say to Her: *"Mother, I have made a mistake, but I am Thy child. Cleanse me and guide me."*
* **Perform Conscious Acts of Kindness:** See the Divine residing in everyone you meet. By offering unconditional kindness and understanding to others, you become a pure channel through which God's love can flow into the world.
* **Use the Power of Devotional Chanting:** Sing to the Lord. Chanting is half the battle in meditation, as it melts the heart and prepares the mind to receive the quiet, subtle vibrations of the Spirit.
* **Maintain Inner Stillness:** Throughout the busy hours of the day, take short, conscious pauses. Take a deep breath, exhale, and mentally repeat: *"Thou and I, Lord, Thou and I."*

### The Guru as the Mirror of God's Love

How do we know that such unconditional love exists in this universe? We see it reflected perfectly in the lives of the great Masters. Paramahansa Yogananda was the very embodiment of that divine compassion. To those of us who had the blessed privilege of living in his presence, he was a constant reminder of God's boundless mercy. 

Master never judged us by our shortcomings. He saw only our divine potential. His love was a protective shield, a guiding light that showed us our true identity as children of the Divine. Through his unconditional love for us, he taught us how to love God, and how to love one another with that same pure, unselfish devotion.

Let us remember that we are never alone. No matter how difficult our path may seem, or how many times we stumble, the loving arms of the Divine Mother are always open to us, waiting to receive us back into our eternal home.

---

### A Closing Prayer and Blessing

*O Divine Mother, beloved Heavenly Father, Friend, and Guru,*  
*May Thy love shine forever on the sanctuary of our devotion, and may we be able to awaken Thy love in all hearts.*  
*Teach us to feel Thy presence in the quiet depths of our meditation, and in the busy moments of our daily lives.*  
*Cleanse our minds of all doubts and fears, and fill our hearts with Thy boundless, unconditional love.*  
*We surrender our lives, our hopes, and our souls into Thy loving hands.*  

*Jai Guru. Jai Ma.*
